blocks.content: A tribunal is a body that exercises judicial or quasi-judicial functions. It is less formal than a court and is designed to handle technical matters requiring subject expertise.
A tribunal is a body that exercises judicial or quasi-judicial functions.

items: Tribunals possess quasi-judicial functions, distinguishing them from ordinary administrative bodies.
The primary distinction between courts and tribunals lies in the degree of formality and the requirement of subject expertise for technical matters.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A tribunal is a body responsible for exercising judicial or quasi-judicial functions.
Compared to traditional courts, tribunals operate in a less formal environment.
Tribunals are specifically designed to address technical matters that demand specialized subject expertise.
